messages.text:
Hey Sarah. What’s the hashrate supposed to be in normal mode? And do u know
the frequency and core voltage for that normal setting?
Note to the team: Routed to Hal, who answers Jack's firmware question in the thread.

Thanks for getting back to me. I have it in normal mode and I’m averaging
around 6 th/s. The preset for normal mode is 455 MHz and 202 for voltage. I
also customized it for 500 MHz and 204 voltage and averaged around 6.5
th/s. I ran both these settings for 24 hours. Can you verify what the
normal preset settings are supposed to be and see if mine is
underperforming? Thanks.
Note to the team: Handed to Hal with Jack's 24-hour figures and screenshots; he replies in the thread.
Hello. Did you ever find anything out about this?
Handed to the team · Per-mode preset spec for the Thor P2 is not in our product data and the customer

Hi Jack,

Nothing new yet, and I am sorry you have had to ask again. I have put your figures straight in front of JD, our hardware specialist: Normal preset at 455 MHz and core voltage 202, 6.05 TH/s averaged over fourteen hours at 63.7 W and 10.5 J/TH, 40.9 degrees on the hashboard, 99.98 percent accepted, confirmed independently by your Datum gateway, plus the 6.5 TH/s you measured at 500 MHz and 204. The question for him is simple: are those the real factory Normal preset values, and is 6.0 TH/s within spec for that preset or short of it.

He is offline this evening and picks it up tomorrow from 10am ET, and his answer comes to you right here in this thread.

If you would rather not wait, JD is on our Discord and usually answers quickly there. The invite is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post in the server and mention @nullhashrate, his handle shows as JD with the Admin role. Either route gets you the same person.

For what it is worth, nothing in your readings looks like a fault. The power draw, the temperature and the share acceptance are all clean, and the clean scaling from 455 to 500 MHz says the chips are healthy. The open question is only what the preset is meant to deliver.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy
No worries, thanks for the update!

Hi Jack,

Thanks for being patient with it. Nothing more is needed from you, JD has everything and his answer comes back to you right here.

In the meantime there is no need to change anything on the miner. Leaving it on the Normal preset at 455 MHz gives him a clean baseline to compare against, and the unit is running cool and accepting shares, so nothing is at risk while it sits there.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy
